authoring.value:
The set $S$ is retained exactly. A nonempty $y$ fiber requires $2\le2xz$, so $xz\ge1$. The inequality $0\le z\le2x$ then forces $x>0$. For a fixed admissible $x$, combine these requirements to obtain

$$\frac1x\le z\le2x.$$

This interval is nonempty precisely when $1/x\le2x$, giving $1/\sqrt2\le x\le2$. Every point in this base admits $2\le y\le2xz$. Thus the full nonempty $z$ fiber has endpoints $a(x)=1/x$ and $b(x)=2x$, with

$$a(x)b(x)=\frac1x(2x)=2.$$

The valid repeated integral is

$$\iiint_S f(x,y,z)\,dV=\int_{1/\sqrt2}^{2}\int_{1/x}^{2x}\int_2^{2xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.$$

For $f=1$, integrating in $y$ and $z$ gives $4x^3-4x+1/x$, hence the volume is

$$[x^4-2x^2+\ln x]_{1/\sqrt2}^{2}=\frac{35}{4}+\frac32\ln2>0.$$

The authentic source solution copied the nominal pair $0,2x$ and reported its product $0$. Its formal repeated integral over $x\in[-2,2]$ includes reversed and empty fibers; for $f=1$ it gives $0$, not the volume of $S$. The full nonempty fiber has endpoint product $2$.
